newsitem.title: FINLAND: Silja targets break-even result in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Silja targets break-even result in 1997.

text.p: Finnish passenger ferry operator Silja Oy Ab said on Wednesday it expected earnings for the current year to reach or exceed break-even.
"The group's favourable trend is expected to continue and it is estimated that earnings for 1997 should be able to attain or exceed the break-even level," Silja said.
Silja said the group's positive operating cash flow would strengthen.
For its Baltic Sea passenger ferry arm Silja Line, it said the earnings improvement was expected to continue.
The results of its English channel passenger ferry operator Sally were expected to "improve significantly as of spring 1997," Silja said, referring to restructuring started last autumn.
Silja said its 1996 result -- a 133 million markka loss after financial items against a 389 million markka loss the previous year -- had improved in line with expectations.
"When assessing the group's result trend it should be born in mind that payments from Wartsila Marine's bankruptcy estate had a positive effect on 1996 results," Silja said.
Group gross revenues at 4.0 billion markka, up from 3.8 billion in 1995, included a 69 million markka payment from the bankruptcy estate, it said.
